idea.why: The decomposition the brief implies, each part a real concern: two specialist readers run independently on raw data, then a third does only synthesis and is explicitly told not to re-list what the specialists already sorted. Empty-input behaviour is designed into each agent rather than left to chance.

structure.why: Right node types throughout: Aggregate bundles items so each agent runs once, the HTML node renders rather than a Code node string-building, structured parsers pin each shape. Two nits: the agents carry no tools so a chain is the purpose-built node, and two model sub-nodes are byte-identical where one shared would cover.

connections.why: The trigger fans out to two genuinely independent branches, each chained through its own aggregate and agent, rejoining at a real Merge that acts as the sync barrier. The facts confirm synthesis depends on both branches while neither depends on the other. Slight indirection: the prompt reads both streams via node references, so the merged payload is effectively unused.

answer.why: End to end what was asked, with every section carrying a written empty state. Held back because the dashboard exists only as an email, and the layout leans on a head style block and flexbox tiles that degrade in stricter mail clients.

appraisal: A well-shaped answer rather than the first thing that compiled: three agents with genuinely distinct jobs, a parallel fetch of the two sources, a real merge where they rejoin, and a synthesis step told to tie the two together instead of restating them. The craft details are unusually good: Aggregate before each agent so the model sees one list rather than N invocations, structured schemas so the template can index fields safely, executeOnce on the tail so a multi-item branch cannot mail three briefings, and an explicit empty state in every section. What it gets wrong is small: the Merge output is never read since the prompt pulls both inputs by reference, the two model sub-nodes are duplicates, and the agents have no tools. A knowledgeable user would change delivery first, adding a webhook-served version so the dashboard is a page you can open.
